title: The for loop
summary: Its three parts, and counting from 1 to n.

say.never: A `for` loop repeats code, and it has three parts inside its parentheses. First **where to start** (`int i = 1`). Then **when to keep going** (`i <= n`). Then **how to step** (`i++` means add 1 each time). The code between the braces runs once for every value of `i`.
say.bit: A `for` loop says where to start, when to keep going, and how to step.

marks.label: keep going while this is true
after each pass, add 1 to i

say.never: The classic loop mistake is `<` versus `<=`. `i < n` stops *before* n, so it misses the last number. `i <= n` includes n. If your answer is always off by one, check this first.
say.bit: The most common loop bug: `<` vs `<=`.

board.code:
for (int i = 1; i < n; i++)   // 1 .. n-1  (misses n)
for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++)  // 1 .. n

say.never: Our team uses `for` loops and avoids `while` loops. A `while` loop that never ends can freeze a robot. A `for` loop makes you say where it ends right at the start, which keeps you safe.
say.bit: Team standard: use `for`, not `while`. A `while` loop that never ends freezes a robot. A `for` loop makes you write the ending up front.
